summary: HIDDEN TRUTH (never ingested). Travis Kemper owed his former business partner Marcus Hale $18,000 and Hale had threatened to sue and expose him. On Saturday 14 March 2026 they agreed to meet at the Riverside Lot. Kemper brought his cousin Rory Vance as a passenger in his gray 2016 Honda Civic SYN4821; they stopped at Calder Fuel & Go (Vance bought drinks and cigarettes), then entered the lot at 22:41:05. Earlier, 22:10-22:19, Hale's brother-in-law Wes Darnell (the red herring) argued with Hale there over a trailer hitch and left in his blue Camry; bus rider Dana Whitfield saw that and later mistook it for the shooting (wrong time 22:15, wrong color blue). At 22:44:20 Kemper shot Hale once with his 9mm pistol after Hale said he was done protecting him. Vance stood by the car and did not shoot. They left at 22:47:30 with headlights off and returned to Larkspur Court at 23:03, where Kemper carried off his dark hooded jacket. The pistol and jacket were never recovered. Kemper was arrested on 16 March and lied in interview that he was alone and never got out of the car.

events.description: Kemper calls Hale (4 min) about the overdue $18,000 loan; Hale gives him until mid-March.
14-minute heated call. Hale threatens to file in small-claims court and to tell Kemper's new employer about the debt. Kemper later admits in interview 'we argued about the money'.
Kemper calls Hale (7 min) and they agree to meet at the Riverside Lot on Saturday night 'around 10:30' so Kemper can hand over a partial payment.
Darnell calls Hale (3 min), angry that Hale still has his trailer hitch and owes him $600. Darnell: 'I'm done waiting, Marc.'
Kemper calls Vance's prepaid phone (2 min) and asks him to ride along 'to see a guy about money'.
Gray Civic SYN4821 read leaving Larkspur Court by the Larkspur/Bayview ALPR with Kemper and Vance aboard.
Kemper calls Hale (62 s): 'I'm on my way, gotta grab gas first.'
Hale's white F-150 SYN7305 enters the Riverside Lot and parks in space C-6, nose toward the levee.
Hale calls Darnell (75 s) from the lot: 'Come get your hitch, I'm at the river lot.'
Darnell's blue Camry SYN2290 enters the lot and stops behind Hale's pickup.

Hale and Darnell argue loudly by the pickup's tailgate; Darnell jabs a finger at Hale, lifts the trailer hitch out of the truck bed and loads it into the Camry trunk. Whitfield watches from the bus shelter.
Camry leaves the lot quickly with a tire squeal (CCTV 22:18:58, ALPR exit read 22:19:02). Whitfield later misremembers this as the 'blue car' fleeing a shooting 'around 10:15'.
Whitfield boards the 10:21 PM Route 9 bus at the shelter on the lot's east edge and leaves the area.
Gray Civic read eastbound at Route 9/Marsh (22:24:37) and pulls up to pump 4 at Calder Fuel & Go.
Darnell's Camry read eastbound at Route 9/Marsh, heading home, 8 minutes after leaving the lot.

Vance (gray cap, olive bomber jacket) goes into the store and pays $14.62 cash for two Volt Surge energy drinks and a pack of Halyard cigarettes (receipt 22:30:58). Kemper, in a dark hooded jacket, pumps $20 of gas and stays by the car.
Gray Civic leaves the station and is read westbound at Route 9/Marsh, back toward the river.
Gray Civic SYN4821 enters the Riverside Lot (CCTV 22:41:05, ALPR 22:41:05) and parks in C-7 beside Hale's pickup at 22:41:40. Ruiz notices it through the market window.

Both occupants get out. The driver (Kemper, dark hood up) walks to Hale at the pickup's tailgate; the passenger (Vance, gray cap) stays by the Civic's rear bumper. Raised voices; Pike, at the fence with his dog, hears 'You'll get it when I have it!' and 'Then I'm done protecting you.'

Kemper fires one 9mm round at close range; Hale falls between the pickup and the Civic. CCTV shows a single muzzle flash at 22:44:20 and the figure dropping. Pike hears 'one loud bang'; Ruiz hears 'a pop like a firecracker'.
Darnell calls Hale's phone from home (served by tower TWR-PC-EAST-07, 9 km east); the call rings out unanswered (0 s). Strong alibi evidence for Darnell.

Both men get back into the Civic; it reverses, idles with headlights off, then leaves fast (CCTV exit 22:47:30, ALPR exit read 22:47:31). Pike sees 'a gray or silver four-door, maybe a Toyota' and partial plate 'SYN 48'; Ruiz sees 'the gray Civic' turn right onto Calder River Road.
Ruiz steps out of the market (CAM-B 22:48:05), runs to Hale, and calls 911 at 22:48:40 (call ~2 min 8 s). She reports a man shot in the Riverside Lot and 'a gray car, like a Civic' leaving.
Officer Nandakumar (unit 2-14) arrives at 22:53:10, finds Hale unresponsive with a single gunshot wound to the chest; paramedics pronounce him dead at 23:01. Scene taped off.
Gray Civic read at Larkspur/Bayview (23:02:48), enters the garage at 23:03:15. Kemper exits carrying a bundled dark jacket under his arm; Vance walks out the pedestrian gate at 23:05:40.
Scene processing: one 9mm cartridge casing (ITEM-001), victim's phone, wallet with $212 (not a robbery), a Halyard cigarette butt and a Volt Surge can by space C-7, tire impression in C-7.
Vance calls Kemper (95 s) from his prepaid phone: (content unknown to police).
Gray Civic read eastbound at Route 9/Marsh just before 1 AM; purpose of the late trip is never established.

Search warrant at unit 14: Civic seized; Fuel & Go receipt (22:30:58) and Halyard pack in the car; empty 9mm pistol box and partial box of 9mm ammunition in the closet; signed $18,000 loan note. Kemper arrested. The pistol and the dark hooded jacket are not found.

Recorded interview in PCPD headquarters interview room 2 (not one of the case locations). Kemper admits the debt and being at the lot but claims he was alone, never got out of the car and left 'before 10:40'.

evidence_plan.title: Recorded interview of Travis Kemper
content_notes: Two TTS voices, room tone, chair creaks. Miranda advisal in the first 20 s.
Kemper admits the debt, the 03-09 argument call and driving to the lot; lies that he was alone and never got out, and that he left 'before 10:40'.
Detective confronts him with the ALPR exit at 22:47:31 and the fuel stop video of a passenger; Kemper goes quiet and asks for a lawyer at ~4:50.

key_lines.text: This is Detective Samuel Brandt, March 16th, 2:10 PM, interview with Travis Kemper.
Marc and me argued about the money, sure. Everybody knew he was on me about it.
I drove over there to give him some cash, he wasn't there, I left. Before 10:40.
I was by myself. I never even got out of the car.
Your car was read leaving that lot at 10:47 PM. And who bought the energy drinks at Fuel and Go?
I'm not saying anything about Rory.
I think I want a lawyer.
